title: Fatimid Caliphate
summary: The Fatimid Caliphate was an Ismaili Shi'i caliphate founded in 909 in Ifriqiya (modern Tunisia) by Abd Allah al-Mahdi Billah, claiming descent from the Prophet Muhammad's daughter Fatima. After expanding across North Africa and the Levant, the Fatimids conquered Egypt and founded Cairo (al-Qahira) as their imperial capital in 969. The dynasty became a major Mediterranean trading and cultural power before Saladin overthrew the caliphate in 1171, restoring Sunni governance in Egypt.

uncertainty.note: Established in 297 AH / 909 CE in Tunisia; overthrown by Saladin in 567 AH / 1171 CE in Cairo.

as_recorded.value: Established in 297/909 in Tunisia, the seat of the Fatimids was later transferred to Egypt in 362/973... overthrown by Salah-al-Din (Saladin) in 567/1171
Cairo was founded as the headquarter of the Fatimid Caliphate in 969 AD.

importance.justification: The Fatimids established the premier Shi'i caliphate in Islamic history, challenging Abbasid authority, founding Cairo, and patronizing major theological and scientific institutions.
